faq.a: We recommend boarding by 23:00 to settle in, get a drink, and secure your spot. The fireworks display usually starts at midnight and lasts 10–15 minutes. After the show, you can cruise back to port and continue the celebration.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a small group on New Year's Eve?
faq.a: For groups of 5–6, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) or Red Tide (11m, 6 pax) are solid choices. For up to 8, the Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) offers more comfort. All depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food or decorations on board?

faq.q: Is there a minimum booking duration for New Year's Eve?

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for New Year's Eve 2031?
faq.a: We recommend booking at least 2–3 months ahead. December is peak season in Marbella, and our fleet of 17 boats fills up quickly. The earlier you book, the more choice you have.

faq.q: Can we watch the fireworks from the boat without docking?
faq.a: Absolutely. The best views are from the water, just outside Puerto Banús. Your skipper will anchor at a safe distance with a clear line of sight to the fireworks. You'll be close enough to hear the bangs and see the reflections on the sea.

data.body_html:
New Year's Eve 2031 in Marbella is the kind of night you remember for a decade. The fireworks explode over Puerto Banús, the yachts line the marina, and everyone is dressed up. But the best seat in the house isn't on land — it's on the water. A New Year's Eve 2031 Marbella yacht charter gives you front-row views of the midnight display, with a licensed skipper, drinks, and snacks included. No crowds, no queues, no rush. Just you, your group, and the reflection of fireworks on the Mediterranean.

Our fleet of 17 boats departs from Puerto Banús, so you're minutes from the action. Whether you want a speedy 2-hour trip on an Azimut 39 or a 4-hour luxury cruise on a Mangusta 80, we've got the boat and the skipper. Below, we break down the best options, the costs, and everything you need to plan the perfect evening.

Why a Yacht Charter Beats the Crowds

Every year, thousands of people pack the promenades of Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina to watch the fireworks. You'll queue for drinks, fight for a spot, and probably spend the final countdown staring at someone's phone screen. On a private yacht, you skip all that. Your skipper anchors just outside the harbour, giving you an unobstructed view of the sky. You've got your own bar, your own music, and your own toilet. No jostling, no cold wind — just the show.

Our Fleet for New Year's Eve 2031

Every boat in our fleet is available for charter on 31 December 2031. Here are the most popular choices for fireworks viewing:

All prices include skipper, fuel, insurance, Spanish VAT (21%), and a selection of drinks and snacks. For Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 white or grey), a jet ski is included free on the 4-hour charter.

The Fireworks Display: What to Expect

The main show kicks off at midnight from the pier at Puerto Banús. It runs for about 12 minutes, with a mix of coloured bursts, silver waterfalls, and grand finales. The best viewing angle is from the water, about 200 metres off the port. Your skipper will position the boat bow-on to the display so everyone on deck gets a clear view. After the fireworks, you can cruise back to the marina, pop open another cava, and watch the celebrations from the dock.

What's Included on Every Charter

No hidden extras. Every booking includes:

  • Licensed skipper (English & Spanish speaking)
  • Fuel for the full charter duration
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (olives, crisps, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You're welcome to bring your own food, decorations, or a playlist. Just let us know in advance if you need a Bluetooth speaker or extra storage.

How to Book Your New Year's Eve 2031 Charter

Booking is straightforward. Visit our boat rental Marbella page to browse the full fleet, then send us a WhatsApp with your preferred boat, date (31 December 2031), and duration. We'll confirm availability and send a payment link. A 50% deposit secures the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure.

For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the price is fixed at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. For Tier B (Mangusta 80), it's €4,719 for 4 hours. All other boats are priced on request — typically between €1,500 and €8,000 depending on size and duration.

Tips for a Perfect New Year's Eve on the Water

  • Dress warmly: December evenings in Marbella average 12–16°C. Bring a jacket or a wrap.
  • Arrive early: Boarding at 23:00 gives you time to settle in before the countdown.
  • Bring sparklers: Many guests like to light sparklers on deck at midnight — just check with the skipper first.
  • Designate a photographer: The fireworks reflect beautifully on the water, so have someone ready with a camera.
  • Book a longer charter: A 4-hour slot (22:00–02:00) gives you time to cruise, watch the show, and enjoy a post-midnight drink on the water.

Why Choose Our Fleet?

We operate 17 boats, all based in Puerto Banús. No third-party listings, no middlemen. You deal directly with the team that maintains the boats. Every vessel is fully insured, regularly serviced, and equipped with safety gear. Our skippers know the coastline from Marbella to Sotogrande and can tailor the route to your preferences. For New Year's Eve, they'll position you perfectly for the fireworks.

If you're considering a longer celebration, check out our New Year's Eve 2031 yacht charter guide for more ideas.

Frequently asked questions

What time should we board for New Year's Eve fireworks?

We recommend boarding by 23:00 to settle in, get a drink, and secure your spot. The fireworks display usually starts at midnight and lasts 10–15 minutes. After the show, you can cruise back to port and continue the celebration.

Which boat is best for a small group on New Year's Eve?

For groups of 5–6, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) or Red Tide (11m, 6 pax) are solid choices. For up to 8, the Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) offers more comfort. All depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper.

Can we bring our own food or decorations on board?

Yes, you're welcome to bring your own food, party decorations, and extra drinks. We provide light snacks and a selection of drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava). Just let us know in advance if you need extra storage space.

What happens if the weather is bad on New Year's Eve?

The captain will assess conditions on the day. If it's unsafe to sail, we offer a full refund or reschedule to another date. Marbella's winter weather is generally mild, with average December sea temperatures around 16°C and calm winds.

Is there a minimum booking duration for New Year's Eve?

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) have a minimum of 2 hours at €749. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80) require a minimum 4-hour charter at €4,719. For other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp.

Do you offer a champagne toast at midnight?

Yes, we provide cava (Spanish sparkling wine) on every charter. If you prefer Champagne or a specific brand, you're welcome to bring your own bottle. No corkage fee.

How far in advance should I book for New Year's Eve 2031?

We recommend booking at least 2–3 months ahead. December is peak season in Marbella, and our fleet of 17 boats fills up quickly. The earlier you book, the more choice you have.

Can we watch the fireworks from the boat without docking?

Absolutely. The best views are from the water, just outside Puerto Banús. Your skipper will anchor at a safe distance with a clear line of sight to the fireworks. You'll be close enough to hear the bangs and see the reflections on the sea.
